I'll read the file first to understand the current code.## Plan

The RAW on `v` carries values between iterations: line 7 in iteration i writes `v[jv[i]]`, which line 6 in iteration j > i needs to read. The key insight is that the profiler reports no WAW on u or v, meaning each location is written at most once—so iteration order does not determine the final values, only which iterations update each location.

**Solution**: split the loop into two sequential passes:
1. First loop: compute all u updates, reading from the (unchanged) initial v
2. Second loop: compute all v updates, reading from the (now-final) u values

This moves the RAW dependence from inside the loop to between two separate loops. Each loop becomes independently parallelizable (Do-All): the first loop has no loop-carried dependence because v is never written within it, and the second loop has no loop-carried dependence because u is frozen (final values). Output is preserved because no iteration writes the same location twice, so the order of updates does not affect final values.
